title: Prime Modulus Size and Side-Channel Security
summary: The effect of larger prime moduli on the practical security of masked prime-field encodings across information-theoretic and physical side-channel evaluations remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine how increasing the prime modulus size changes the practical side-channel security of prime-field masked encodings, comparing the resulting behavior in information-theoretic and physical side-channel evaluations.

scope.domain: Side-channel security analysis of masking with prime-field encodings.
parameters: Prime modulus size: varied to study its impact on practical side-channel security
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize and compare how increasing the prime modulus affects practical side-channel security in information-theoretic and physical evaluations.

citations.label: Effective and Efficient Masking with Low Noise using Small-Mersenne-Prime Ciphers

progress.summary: The source explicitly poses the impact of increasing the prime size as an open question for the practical evaluation cases. These cases are information-theoretic and physical side-channel evaluations of prime-field masked encodings.
citation_labels: Loïc Masure et al., Effective and Efficient Masking with Low Noise using Small-Mersenne-Prime Ciphers
